user_scenario: You are Teodora Brinkmann, owner of Dunewood Coffee Roasters LLC in Grand Haven, Michigan — friendly, chatty, and calling from the roastery between batches. The company is opening a second roasting plant at 6860 Hayes St in Spring Lake, whose electric service is scheduled to start on November 2, and you want its security deposit set up today so nothing holds up the opening. You open by saying exactly that, and that you are the owner and can act for the company; you are happy for the representative to record whatever deposit Lakeshore's rules call for on the new plant. When asked how to find the account you give the company's phone number on file, 6164318826. Only when the representative asks to verify the account do you give the last four digits of the company's EIN, 4791; if one more detail is wanted you give the billing email, books@dunewoodcoffee.com, or the billing ZIP code, 49417. You do not know Lakeshore's deposit rules, figures or internal steps, and you never suggest an amount, a date or a number of installments. If the representative explains that the plant's deposit cannot be set until a payment has been received on the deposit already set for the new cafe on Savidge Street, you agree and say you will make whatever payment the representative sets out on that deposit yourself, right now; when the representative hands that payment over to you, you make it exactly as set out to you — the deposit reference, the installment number, the number of installments and the amount. If the representative tells you the roastery's deposit has come through its two-year review and will be returned, you are delighted and ask for it as a check, mailed to the address on file. If asked whether the new plant has a reference letter from another utility or any other reason to skip its deposit, you say no, it does not. If the representative offers to take a surety bond or a letter of credit instead of cash for the new plant, you say cash is fine. Once the representative confirms the new plant's deposit has been set up, you note the amount, thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The new-agreement assessment has two parallel prerequisites, the roastery refund (step 10) and the cafe opening installment (step 12). They write different deposits (the refund books a deposit_refund row on the roastery deposit and sets it refunded; the installment books a deposit_payment row on the cafe deposit and sets its installment_count and held_amount) and neither reads anything the other writes: the refund computation reads only the roastery deposit's ledger and the roastery's service records, the installment computation only the cafe deposit's recorded amounts and the customer's notices, reversals and bills. Running them in the order installment then refund gives the identical terminal state and the identical values 2929.93, 951.89 and 7954.00 (checked with the authoring replay). Skipping the refund leaves the roastery deposit held: the good-payment relief falls to refund_relief_part 0.25 (held, fully secured 24 months) and the plant's required deposit becomes 8837.00 instead of 7954.00; the terminal state also lacks the 2929.93 check refund.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — security_deposits task 1 (Dunewood Coffee Roasters LLC: new Hayes Street plant deposit).

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]}. Occupied by task 0: deposit_ext_failed_review_extension, deposit_ext_anniversary_interest, deposit_ext_recalculated_requirement, deposit_ext_additional_installment and their four tools. Claimed here (whole tree, no overlap): deposit_ext_review_refund (4 factors, refund_deposit_by_check_703d791f, agent), deposit_ext_opening_installment (4 factors, pay_deposit_installment_d7ce4a9b, owner=user), deposit_ext_new_agreement_requirement (6 factors, assess_new_service_deposit_5e8da269, agent). Task 1 is the last task, so after it every extended policy of the charter is claimed exactly once.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only to set up the deposit for a plant that is not yet in service. The new-agreement policy states two waits in its own rule: the deposit is not fixed until every other assessed deposit of the customer shows its first installment received (the Savidge Street cafe deposit, assessed 2026-09-29, has nothing received), and it is fixed only after any deposit whose review has been passed on its review date has been refunded (the roastery deposit's 24-month review falls today and passes). The agent must discover both, work the cafe's opening installment (customer pays, 6-installment plan, front share by the pending stage), refund the roastery deposit by check with the closing year's interest under the Commission's year-split rates, and only then size the plant's deposit from the roastery's recent load, the heating difference, the customer-wide record, the established sister and the good-payment relief that the refund just earned. Difficulty is reading the two prerequisite sentences, reconciling three agreements' bills/charges/notices and two deposit ledgers, and computing three multi-factor values; there is one tool per problem.

2. BLUEPRINT DEFECTS AND GATE CONSTRAINTS ROUTED AROUND.
